samples.summary: Redirect-guard tests cannot detect removal of `redirect: 'manual'` — the stub fetch ignores the init argument entirely
samples.evidence: The whole per-hop SSRF guard in `createImageFetcher` (packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:221) depends on passing `{ redirect: 'manual' }` so the loop, not `fetch`, owns the hop. Every test in `describe('createImageFetcher')` (lines 186-341) uses a stub `typeof globalThis.fetch` that only reads `input` and unconditionally returns a synthetic 301/302 `Response`; none of them assert anything about the second argument. If `redirect: 'manual'` were dropped, the stub would still hand back the 302, the loop would still re-check the Location, and 're-checks the target of a redirect instead of following it blindly' would still pass — while real `fetch` would silently auto-follow to `http://169.254.169.254/...` with no check in between. Nothing in the suite pins the option (grep for `redirect` in packages/cli/test returns no assertion).

samples.summary: The `WAFFLEBASE_IMAGE_HOSTS` env wiring in `createImageFetcher` is never exercised end to end
samples.evidence: `parseAllowedHosts` is unit-tested (image-fetcher.test.ts:9-18) and `assertFetchableImageUrl` is tested with an explicit `allowedHosts` array (lines 140-160), but no test sets `process.env.WAFFLEBASE_IMAGE_HOSTS` and drives `createImageFetcher` without `opts.allowedHosts`. The line that joins the two (`opts.allowedHosts ?? parseAllowedHosts(process.env[IMAGE_HOSTS_ENV])`) is the operator-facing escape hatch the error message advertises, and it could be wired to the wrong variable name with the suite green.

samples.summary: `MAX_UPSTREAM_CODE` truncation of an oversized `error.code` has no test
samples.evidence: `safeEnvelope` slices the upstream `code` to 80 chars, but upstream-error.test.ts only covers the 500-char message cap (line 130) and the 4000-byte body cap (line 139). Grep for `MAX_UPSTREAM_CODE` / a long-code fixture in packages/cli/test returns nothing, so removing the `.slice(0, MAX_UPSTREAM_CODE)` would not fail any test.

samples.summary: `moveDocument` and `uploadImageFile` got `seg()` but are excluded from the new encoding test matrices
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/api/url.test.ts enumerates share-links, folders, workspaces, datasources, analytics, miro and files, and documents.test.ts:104 covers fetch/rename/copy/delete — but `moveDocument` (documents.ts:88) and `uploadImageFile` (app/spreadsheet/image-upload.ts:48) are in neither list. Their existing tests (documents.test.ts `moveDocuments` bulk endpoint, image-upload.test.ts) assert nothing about id encoding, so a regression on those two call sites would go unnoticed.

samples.summary: `downloadFileDocument`'s switch from `encodeURIComponent` to `seg()` (the dot-segment refusal) is untested
samples.evidence: The 'refuses a dot segment instead of walking up one level' test in upstream-error.test.ts only exercises `deleteDocument('..')` and `getCell('doc-1','tab-1','.')`. `downloadFileDocument` is the one call site whose behavior actually changed (it already percent-encoded; the new part is the throw), and no test calls it with `.`/`..`. files-download.test.ts asserts only on `resolveDownloadTarget` and the io path.
searchedFor: read packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts 'request paths pin every id' block

finding.summary: Redirect-guard tests cannot detect removal of `redirect: 'manual'` — the stub fetch ignores the init argument entirely
finding.evidence: The whole per-hop SSRF guard in `createImageFetcher` (packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:221) depends on passing `{ redirect: 'manual' }` so the loop, not `fetch`, owns the hop. Every test in `describe('createImageFetcher')` (lines 186-341) uses a stub `typeof globalThis.fetch` that only reads `input` and unconditionally returns a synthetic 301/302 `Response`; none of them assert anything about the second argument. If `redirect: 'manual'` were dropped, the stub would still hand back the 302, the loop would still re-check the Location, and 're-checks the target of a redirect instead of following it blindly' would still pass — while real `fetch` would silently auto-follow to `http://169.254.169.254/...` with no check in between. verdict.reason: Verified independently: image-fetcher.ts:221 passes `{ redirect: 'manual' }`, and the source comment (lines 215-218) states the per-hop SSRF guard depends on it. All eight stub fetches in describe('createImageFetcher') (test lines 188, 210, 227, 244, 262, 287, 313, 330) declare signatures that take only `input` (or nothing) and unconditionally return synthetic 301/302/200 Responses; none accept or assert the `init` argument. Deleting `redirect: 'manual'` therefore cannot fail any test — the stubs never auto-follow either way. Searched wide for a counterexample and found none: repo-wide grep for `createImageFetcher` shows the only other consumers are production code (commands/docs.ts:261, commands/slides.ts:209); repo-wide grep for `manual` across packages/**/*.ts finds `redirect: 'manual'` only at the source line, in no test/helper/fixture; no real-HTTP integration test exists in packages/cli (grep for createServer/listen matched only src/commands/login.ts); and the only RequestInit assertions in packages/cli/test are in upstream-error.test.ts:449-472 against the API client, not the image fetcher. This is a real behavior (the hop-ownership option guarding against 302 -> 169.254.169.254) shipped with no assertion pinning it, while the test titled 're-checks the target of a redirect instead of following it blindly' presents itself as coverage — a missing-test gap in this lens's lane.
